questions.q_en: Who presides over the sessions of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution_en:
● Under Article 63, the Vice President of India acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

● The Prime Minister, President, and Speaker of Lok Sabha do not preside over Rajya Sabha sessions.

Further Insight:

● The President is the Head of the Union and mentioned under Article 52.

● The Prime Minister is the Head of the Council of Ministers whose duty is to aid and advise the president while the President exercises his power under Article 74.

● Speaker of Lok Sabha is the presiding officer of the Lok Sabha or House of People and mentioned in Article 93 of the Constitution.

Consider the following statements about the Houses of Parliament.

a. Rajya Sabha is directly elected by the people of India.

questions.solution_en:

• Members of Lok Sabha shall be directly elected by members of the constituencies in the States

○ with 530 members representing the States and 20 representing the Union Territories.

○ At present, the Lok Sabha has 543 seats filled by elected representatives.

• The Rajya Sabha should consist of not more than 250 members -

○ 238 members representing the States and Union Territories,

○ and 12 members nominated by the President.

○ Current Strength of Rajya Sabha is 245

questions.q_en: Which of the following is incorrect about Qualification for Member of Lok Sabha or House of the People?
options_en: Candidate must be citizen of India
Candidate must attain minimum age of 25 years
Candidate should not hold office of profit under Government of India
Candidate must be born in India
questions.solution_en:
• Qualifications for Lok Sabha (House of the People) - Article 84:

○ The candidate must be a citizen of India.

○ The minimum age required is 25 years.

○ The candidate must be registered as a voter in any parliamentary constituency in India.

○ The candidate should not hold any office of profit under the Government of India or any state, except for offices specifically exempted by Parliament.

○ The candidate must not be disqualified under Article 102, which includes:

■ Being declared of unsound mind by a competent court.

■ Being an undischarged insolvent.

■ Being disqualified under laws made by Parliament, such as those related to criminal offenses (e.g., Representation of the People Act, 1951).

Which of the following statements is correct for the reason of disqualification of a member of Rajya Sabha under Article 102?

a. If he holds office of Profit under the Government of India or any State

b. If he is undischarged insolvent

c. If he voluntarily acquired citizenship of a foreign State
questions.solution_en:
• Article 102: Disqualification for membership

○ (1) A person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a member of either House of Parliament

■ (a) if he holds any office of profit under the Government of India or the Government of any State, other than an office declared by Parliament by law not to disqualify its holder

■ if he is of unsound mind and stands so declared by a competent court;

■ if he is an undischarged insolvent;

■ if he is not a citizen of India, or has voluntarily acquired the citizenship of a foreign State, or is under any acknowledgment of allegiance or adherence to a foreign State;

■ if he is so disqualified by or under any law made by Parliament.

○ (2) A person shall be disqualified for being a member of either House of Parliament if he is so disqualified under the Tenth Schedule.

• Qualifications for Rajya Sabha (Council of States) - Article 84:

○ The candidate must be a citizen of India.

○ The minimum age required is 30 years.

○ The candidate must be a registered voter in any state or Union Territory in India.

○ Similar to Lok Sabha, the candidate should not hold any office of profit under the Government of India or any state, unless specifically exempted by Parliament.

○ Candidate must not be disqualified under Article 102

questions.q_en: The Rajya Sabha can delay a money bill for_________.
questions.solution_en:
• The Rajya Sabha can delay a money bill for a maximum of 14 days. It cannot amend or reject it.

Further Insight:

• Money Bill

o It is defined under Article 110

o A bill can be deemed as money bill if

a) The imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of any tax

b) Any guarantee or financial obligation by Government of India for Payment of money or withdrawal of money from Consolidated Fund of India or Contingency Fund of India or Their custody.

c) Appropriation of Moneys out of the Consolidated fund of India.

d) Any Expenditure Charged on Consolidated fund of India

o It can only be introduced in the House of People or Lok Sabha.

o Rajya Sabha can only discuss the money bill and give recommendation

o These recommendations are not binding to Lok Sabha

o Rajya Sabha can hold the bill for a period of 14 days only ,after that it automatically passes.

o The Speaker of the Lok Sabha stamped the bill as the money bill.

o Budget is the Money bill

questions.q_en: Who acts as the presiding officer of the Legislative Assembly?
questions.solution_en:
• The Speaker acts as the presiding officer of the Legislative Assembly.

• The Deputy Speaker acts in the absence of the Speaker.

Further Insight:

• Article 178 governs the election, duties, and removal of the Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly.

• The Speaker plays a crucial role in maintaining the order of the Assembly, certifying money bills, and casting votes in the event of a tie.

• The Speaker's decision on parliamentary procedures and the certification of money bills is final and binding.

• The process of removing the Speaker requires a special resolution with 14 days' notice.

questions.q_en: The creation of a State Legislative Council requires:
options_en: A resolution passed by the State Legislature and permission by Parliament
questions.solution_en:
The Legislative Council of a state can be created or abolished by the Parliament based on a recommendation from the state.

• The State Legislature can propose but not create it.

• The Governor recommends but does not establish it.

• The Supreme court has no direct power in this regard.

Further insight:

• Legislative Councils Abolition or creation(Article 169) Procedure:

o Only Parliament of India can create or abolish Legislative council if State Legislative Assembly pass a resolution for abolition or creation by majority of 2/3rd present and voting

questions.q_en: A money bill can be introduced in the Legislative Assembly only with the prior recommendation of:

• The Chief Minister may initiate the process of Money bill, but the bill requires the Governor's recommendation.

• The Advocate General has no role in money bills.

• The Speaker presides over discussions but does not recommend bills.

Further insight

• Money Bill is mentioned under Article 199

• A bill can be deemed as money bill if

(a) the imposition, abolition, remission, alteration, or regulation of any tax;

(b) the regulation of the borrowing of money or the giving of any guarantee by the State, or the amendment of the law with respect to any financial obligations undertaken or to be undertaken by the State;

(c) the custody of the Consolidated Fund or the Contingency Fund of the State, the payment of moneys into or the withdrawal of moneys from any such Fund;

(d) the appropriation of moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of the State;

(e) the declaring of any expenditure to be expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State, or the increasing of the amount of any such expenditure;

(f) the receipt of money on account of the Consolidated Fund of the State or the public account of the State or the custody or issue of such money

• It can only be introduced in the State legislative Assembly, not in the State Legislative Council.

• State legislative Council can only discuss the money bill and give recommendation

• These recommendations are not binding to Lok Sabha

• The State Legislative Council can hold a bill for a period of 14 days only ,after that it automatically passes.

• The Speaker of the State Legislative Council stamped the bill as the money bill.

• The budget is the Money bill.

• The Chief Minister may initiate the process of Money bill, but the bill requires the Governor's recommendation.

• The Advocate General has no role in money bills.

• The Speaker presides over discussions but does not recommend bills.

Further insight

• Money Bill is mentioned under Article 199

• A bill can be deemed as money bill if

(a) the imposition, abolition, remission, alteration, or regulation of any tax;

(b) the regulation of the borrowing of money or the giving of any guarantee by the State, or the amendment of the law with respect to any financial obligations undertaken or to be undertaken by the State;

(c) the custody of the Consolidated Fund or the Contingency Fund of the State, the payment of moneys into or the withdrawal of moneys from any such Fund;

(d) the appropriation of moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of the State;

(e) the declaring of any expenditure to be expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State, or the increasing of the amount of any such expenditure;

(f) the receipt of money on account of the Consolidated Fund of the State or the public account of the State or the custody or issue of such money

• It can only be introduced in the State legislative Assembly, not in the State Legislative Council.

• State legislative Council can only discuss the money bill and give recommendation

• These recommendations are not binding to Lok Sabha

• The State Legislative Council can hold a bill for a period of 14 days only ,after that it automatically passes.

• The Speaker of the State Legislative Council stamped the bill as the money bill.

• The budget is the Money bill.

questions.q_en: What proportion of Legislative Council members are elected by graduates?
questions.solution_en:
• As per article 171, 1/12th of the member of the council shall be elected by graduates.

Further Insight:

• The minimum strength of the Legislative Council is set at 40 members but cannot exceed 1/3rd of the total number of members in Legislative Assembly of the State.

• Members are elected from different constituencies:

○ 1/3 are elected by the members of the Legislative Assembly.

○ 1/3 are elected by local authorities (municipalities, district boards, etc.).

○ 1/12 are elected by teachers in the state.

○ 1/12 are elected by graduates of the state.

○ The remaining members are nominated by the Governor for their expertise in fields like literature, science, arts, social service and co-operative movement.

• The members of the State Legislative Council serve a term of six years, with one-third of the members retiring every two years, making the Council a permanent body.

questions.q_en: The State Legislature consists of _______, _______ and in some states _________ is also present .
options_en: President, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
Governor, State Legislative Assembly and State Council
Governor, State Council and State Legislative Assembly
Governor, State Legislative Assembly and Chief Minister
questions.solution_en:
• In State, State Legislature is made up of:

■ State Legislative Assembly (Article 168) + Governor

■ State Legislative Assembly + Governor + Legislative Council(169).

■ State legislative council is presently in Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka ,Tamil Nadu , Telangana and Uttar Pradesh

• Legislative Councils Abolition or creation(Article 169) Procedure:

■ o Only Parliament of India can create or abolish Legislative council if State Legislative Assembly pass a resolution for abolition or creation by majority of 2/3rd present and voting.

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements regarding the discretionary powers of the Governor:

a. The Governor can reserve any bill for the President's consideration.

b. The Governor has the power to dismiss the Chief Minister at their discretion.

c. The Governor can act without the advice of the Council of Ministers in certain circumstances.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution_en:
• The Governor can reserve any bill for the President's consideration under Article 200 of the Constitution.

• The Governor cannot dismiss the Chief Minister at their discretion. The Chief Minister must resign if they lose the majority in the Legislative Assembly.

• In some situations (e.g., when reserving a bill for the President), the Governor can act without the advice of the Council of Ministers.

Further Insight:

• Discretionary power of the Governor in the Article 163

• Article 163(1) Council of Ministers to aid and advise the governor to exercise his function except so far as he is by or under constitution required to exercise his function or any of them at his discretion.

• Article 163(2) If there is a question if he can use his discretion under the Constitution, the decision of the Governor in his discretion shall be final and validity of anything done by the Governor shall not be called in question on the ground that he ought or ought not to have acted in his discretion.
